inputs.original_text: Micheál Martin is pointing to increased housing tenancies, but that doesn’t erase the more urgent reality: eviction notices and homelessness are rising, and the number of people in emergency accommodation has increased again. The Government’s six-year lease rules, introduced on March 1, are being discussed as a backdrop to this crisis—but headline tenancy growth is no substitute for protecting people from losing their homes. A housing system should be judged by whether people can stay safely housed, not by numbers that obscure those being pushed into homelessness.
inputs.modified_text: Micheál Martin can point to more tenancies, but that statistic means little if people are still being pushed out of their homes. Eviction notices, homelessness and the number of people in emergency accommodation are all rising. The six-year lease rules introduced on March 1 are being discussed against that backdrop, but a housing system that leaves people without secure homes is failing them. We should judge policy by whether renters—especially those most vulnerable to displacement—can stay housed, not by headline figures that hide their insecurity.
